learningObjectives: Explain the macOS host requirement in the TMA 2025.4 iOS support matrix.
Prepare a physical iOS device: Developer Mode, trust settings, and cabling.
Launch and use the iOS Simulator through Xcode as an automation target.
Distinguish the device identifier from the installed application BundleID.

elements.description: The TMA 2025.4 support matrix lists macOS as the supported iOS host and requires matching Xcode support for iOS 17+ devices. Use a Mac Agent host for this documented setup; Tosca Commander may connect to that host remotely.

elements.text: This is a version-specific supported topology, not a universal claim about every iOS automation product. Some Agent preparation pages retain Windows instructions; do not treat those as overriding the 2025.4 support matrix without vendor confirmation.

bulletPoints: Follow the version-specific iOS host matrix; confirm inconsistent legacy instructions with the vendor.

elements.title: iOS device prerequisites
items: Pair the device with Xcode and enable Developer Mode under Privacy & Security when required. Restart and confirm activation on the device.
Connect to the Mac and accept the device’s Trust prompt when requested.
Confirm the connected device in Xcode and complete the Agent configuration for its iOS version, including UI automation and Web Inspector when applicable.

For physical-device automation, follow the documented Apple team ID, certificate and provisioning-profile workflow. Do not assume that an installed app eliminates driver-signing requirements or that every account type is sufficient.

elements.text: Apple documents that pairing makes Developer Mode available in Settings; an attempted app run is not the only trigger. Development-signed installation can also expose the setting. Ordinary App Store/TestFlight installation is a different workflow.

bulletPoints: Pair, enable Developer Mode when required, restart and confirm activation.
Complete device trust and the Agent’s version-specific signing/configuration steps.

elements.description: Simulator supports development and UI checks on a Mac, but it does not reproduce all physical-device features or performance. Simulated biometric success/failure responses are different from validating real biometric hardware. Use real devices for hardware and performance evidence.

elements.title: Launching a simulator
items: Install compatible Xcode platform support and a simulator runtime; current Xcode uses Components settings, while older versions may use Platforms.
Start the chosen simulator with Xcode’s available device tools and use an application build made for Simulator.
Run the Agent and verify that the simulator is usable and detected. Follow its version-specific team ID requirements for test execution; mirroring alone is not the same workflow.

bulletPoints: Simulator coverage is useful but cannot certify physical-device behavior or performance.
Use a Simulator-compatible app build and the documented Agent execution configuration.

elements.description: Keep the target device or simulator identifier separate from the application identifier. Select and confirm the intended target in Xcode/Agent device management; do not substitute an app’s BundleID for the device identifier.

BundleID identifies the installed iOS application to open. Tosca’s iOS opening method does not require Android AppActivity; the device connection and automation driver still need their own configuration.

elements.text: Use BundleID for an installed iOS app. Application Path is the alternative installation method: .ipa for a physical device and .app for Simulator. Obtain a build for the correct target rather than treating a physical-device IPA as a Simulator application.

bulletPoints: Device selection and application selection are separate.
BundleID identifies an installed iOS app; Application Path supplies a target-compatible installation build.

examPitfalls.title: Trying to run iOS automation from a Windows-only setup
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Installing TMA on Windows and expecting to scan an iOS device or simulator.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For TMA 2025.4, follow the macOS-only iOS host matrix and matching Xcode requirements. A Windows Tosca Commander can connect to a separately configured Mac Agent; this does not imply Commander itself runs on macOS.

examPitfalls.title: Not finding the Developer Mode toggle
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Searching Settings → Privacy & Security on a fresh iOS 16+ device and not seeing Developer Mode at all.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Initiate pairing with Xcode, then enable Developer Mode in Settings when required, restart and confirm activation. Do not assume an attempted application run is the only way to make the setting appear.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming BundleID needs a paired 'activity' value like Android
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Looking for an iOS equivalent of AppActivity when configuring Open Mobile App.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: BundleID identifies the installed iOS app without Android AppActivity. Device connection and signing configuration are still required separately.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which host setup follows the TMA 2025.4 iOS support matrix?

options.text: Apple licensing forbids automation tools from running on other operating systems.
Use a macOS Agent host, with the appropriate Xcode support for the device version.
TMA has no Windows installer at all.
iOS devices can only be charged from a Mac's USB port.

practiceQuiz.rationale: The 2025.4 matrix lists macOS for iOS hosting. A remote Mac Agent can serve a Windows Tosca Commander. This is not a claim that every iOS automation tool and release uses an identical topology.

optionExplanations.A: The support matrix, not a blanket licensing claim, specifies this host setup.
optionExplanations.B: macOS is the documented iOS host in the checked TMA release.
optionExplanations.C: TMA has Windows support for other documented scenarios.
optionExplanations.D: Charging capability does not determine the automation host.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Developer Mode is missing from Settings before an iPhone is paired with Xcode. Which documented preparation step should the learner try?

options.text: Developer Mode was removed in iOS 17.
Initiate Xcode pairing, then check Privacy & Security and complete the activation prompts.
The device needs to be jailbroken first.
Developer Mode is only available on iPads, not iPhones.

practiceQuiz.rationale: Apple documents pairing as a trigger for Developer Mode availability. Activation requires a restart and confirmation. A failed app launch is not a necessary first step.

optionExplanations.A: The missing setting does not show removal from iOS.
optionExplanations.B: Xcode pairing is a documented way to expose Developer Mode.
optionExplanations.C: Jailbreaking is not part of the documented preparation.
optionExplanations.D: Developer Mode is not restricted to iPads.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the iOS equivalent of Android's AppPackage, used to tell Open Mobile App which installed app to launch?
practiceQuiz.rationale: BundleID selects the installed iOS app. It does not replace device selection, connection configuration or signing requirements. AppActivity is the Android field.

optionExplanations.A: This identifies the target device, not the app.
optionExplanations.B: This is the installed iOS application identifier.
optionExplanations.C: This is an Android application field.
optionExplanations.D: A provisioning profile authorizes deployment; it is not the app-selection field.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which validation needs physical-device evidence rather than relying on Simulator UI behavior?

options.text: Real biometric sensor behavior and physical-device performance.

practiceQuiz.hint: Simulating an authentication result does not exercise a physical sensor.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Simulator does not reproduce every hardware feature or physical-device performance. It can support UI checks and simulated biometric results, but those do not validate the real sensor.

optionExplanations.A: Basic UI interactions can be exercised in Simulator.
optionExplanations.B: Real sensors and physical-device performance need physical-device evidence.
optionExplanations.D: App-screen navigation alone does not require hardware validation.

quickRecap.value: Use the TMA 2025.4 macOS iOS host matrix; confirm version-specific Xcode support.
Pair and trust the device, enable Developer Mode when required, and configure Agent signing.
Pairing can expose the setting; restart and confirm activation after enabling it.
Use compatible platform support and a Simulator build; simulated behavior is not physical-device evidence.
Select and verify the device/simulator separately from the application.
BundleID selects the installed iOS app without Android AppActivity.
BundleID opens an installed app; Application Path installs a target-compatible .ipa or .app.

platformVersion: TMA 2025.4 / Tosca 2026.1 LTS; Apple documentation checked 2026-10-06
